title: Chondrocyte Isolation from Human Cartilage
author: Sarah Snelling
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8uphwvn

steps.title: Prepare collagenase solution
steps.instruction: Make a 1 mg ml⁻¹ collagenase solution in standard medium, allow it to dissolve, then sterile‑filter sequentially through a 0.45 µm and a 0.2 µm syringe filter; aliquot and store at –20 °C (use fresh or freeze for up to 6 months, avoiding repeated freeze‑thaw cycles).

steps.title: Wash cartilage pieces in PBS
steps.instruction: Wash the cartilage‑bone cut in PBS by shaking for 1 minute, then repeat the wash once more.

substeps.instruction: Shake cartilage‑bone cut in PBS for 1 minute.
Repeat the PBS wash for another 1 minute.

steps.title: Remove extraneous tissue
steps.instruction: Place the cartilage‑bone cut on a sterile cutting board and, using a clean scalpel, scrape off any remaining blood or non‑cartilage tissue from the cartilage surface.

steps.title: Mince cartilage into small pieces
steps.instruction: Cut full‑thickness cartilage pieces from the bone surface, place them in standard medium in a petri dish, then mince them with a scalpel into approximately 3 mm × 3 mm × full‑thickness fragments.

steps.title: Digest cartilage with collagenase
steps.instruction: Transfer the minced cartilage pieces into a 50 ml tube containing collagenase digestion mix at a 10 % v/v cartilage‑to‑digestion‑mix ratio; incubate for 12–15 hours at 37 °C with shaking at 45–60 rpm.

steps.title: Filter digested mixture
steps.instruction: After digestion, pass the mixture through a 70 µm cell sieve to remove undigested debris.

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension for 5 minutes at 300 × g, discard supernatant, wash the pellet with standard medium, resuspend, and repeat centrifugation under the same conditions.

substeps.instruction: Discard supernatant and wash pellet with standard medium.

steps.title: Resuspend and adjust cell concentration
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in 1 ml standard medium until fully dispersed, then bring the volume up to 10 ml and mix thoroughly by pipetting; count cells and adjust to a final concentration of 4 × 10⁴ cells ml⁻¹ in standard medium.

steps.title: Plate cells for adhesion
steps.instruction: Dispense 10 ml of the cell‑media suspension into the appropriate number of 10 cm cell‑culture‑treated petri dishes and incubate for 3–7 days at 37 °C in a CO₂ incubator to allow adhesion.

steps.title: Maintain culture and refresh media
steps.instruction: After adhesion (3–7 days), replace media and thereafter refresh media every 2–3 days until cultures reach ~80 % confluence.

steps.title: Freeze cells for storage
steps.instruction: Wash adherent cells with standard medium, scrape off ~5 ml per plate, centrifuge in 15 ml tubes, resuspend the pellet in ice‑cold 10 % DMSO in FBS, and freeze immediately.

steps.title: Passage cells for expansion
steps.instruction: Alternatively, wash cells with standard medium, scrape off ~5 ml per plate, centrifuge in 15 ml tubes, then resuspend in enough medium to split the culture 1:2 (each 10 cm dish becomes two 10 cm dishes); use cells at this passage.
